title: population fanout policy sculptor for staged model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a configurable policy compiler (Population Fanout Policy Sculptor) that translates high-level staged rollout intent into concrete traffic-split plans, step schedules, cohort selectors, and guardrail predicates for the Serving Runtime. The goal is to support flexible patterns across canary/A-B/shadow traffic: fractional splits by cohort, timeboxed steps, adaptive pauses on metric regressions, automatic progressive rollback, and readable simulation output for SRE and PM review.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL accepts a staged rollout manifest and emits a deterministic time-series of traffic splits by route and cohort
Compiled policy integrates with runtime routing layer and can be applied without a runtime restart
Guardrail predicates (latency, error rate, quality delta) configurable per step and per cohort
Abort and auto-rollback triggers have test harness and are exercised via end-to-end simulation
Operator can preview rollout plan in Console (visual step timeline + expected traffic distribution)
definition_of_done: API and UX for creating a staged rollout manifest documented in Console spec
Backend compiler implemented with unit tests and property-based tests for schedule correctness
E2E simulation harness that replays historical telemetry to validate guardrail thresholds
Integration PR merged and feature-flag gated behind rollout-policy-experiment
Confluence runbook for troubleshooting and rolling forward/backwards published
discussion: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting notes — alignment on use cases: quick canary (5 -> 50 -> 100), cohort-limited A/B, shadow probing with shadow sampling 1% -> 5%
2026-03-05: Engineering design review — proposed DSL has 'steps' (duration or % of traffic), 'cohorts' (selector expressions), 'guards' (metric comparisons with windowed baselines)
2026-03-09: Trade-off: simple fixed schedules vs adaptive progression. Decided to support both: fixed steps by default + optional adaptive progression mode with hysteresis to avoid oscillation
2026-03-10: Security flagged need for audit logs of all policy evaluations and decisions — added hook for audit events to be emitted to observability pipeline
2026-03-12: UX review (Lin Chen) — requested a compact text preview and expanded timeline visualization. Agreed to ship text preview first, timeline in next iteration
2026-03-13: PR feedback from runtime team (Ruth Walker) — ensure compiled policy declares compatible model variants for automatic fallback; added 'compatible_variants' field to compiler output
implementation_notes: Compiler will be implemented in Rust component in runtime-scheduler repo; output is a compact JSON plan consumed by router service
Use a deterministic pseudorandom assignment for cohort sampling to keep traffic split stable across restarts
Metric windows use exponentially weighted moving averages (EWMA) for fast reaction while smoothing noise
Auto-rollback holds state in rollout-engine (KVs) with tombstone markers for auditability
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy metrics cause premature rollbacks — mitigation: require two consecutive windows breach before rollback
Risk: misconfigured cohort selector snaps large traffic unexpectedly — mitigation: validators with human-readable warnings and 'preview' enforcement
Risk: performance overhead in router for per-request cohort evaluation — mitigation: precompile per-route hash ranges and use SIMD-friendly checks
notes: Next steps: prototype compiler, add simulation harness, schedule joint runtime/console integration spike (week of 2026-03-16)
PM acceptance criteria to include example manifests for three canonical flows: quick canary, cohort A/B, shadow probe
